title: Machine learning prediction of depression, anxiety, and stress among university students during wartime in Lebanon
summary_en: Predicts depression, anxiety and stress in 225 university students during the 2024 war with a survey (PHQ-9, GAD-7, PSS-10) and nine supervised algorithms. Balanced random forest and AdaBoost perform best; sleep, diet, physical activity, social media use, coping and fear for safety are key predictors.

title: Construction of a multi-source data integration learning decision framework for college students’ mental health
summary_en: Proposes MSDIL-MH, a framework that integrates academic performance, attendance, internet use, social contacts and psychological tests with deep reinforcement learning for early risk detection. Reports higher accuracy than single-source methods without describing the dataset.

title: Identification and validation of an explainable screening model of college students’ mental health with therapeutic strategy implications
summary_en: Develops an explainable depression screening model with 100,257 college students (data from the COVID-19 campus lockdown), comparing 13 algorithms. XGBoost performs best (AUC 0.887); SHAP shows anxiety as the main risk factor and resilience as protective.

title: Reinforcement learning and neural network-driven student psychological crisis intervention strategy
summary_en: Proposes IFF-DDPG, combining a neural network for psychological crisis risk with a reinforcement learning agent that optimises interventions, on a 5,800-record dataset. Reports 97.68% accuracy and post-intervention reductions in stress, anxiety and depression.

title: A multimodal fairness aware machine learning framework for mental health risk prediction in university students
summary_en: Presents BD-MHAM, a multimodal framework (psychological assessments, academic records, digital behaviour, physiology, environment and EMA) with a fairness-constrained ensemble, tested on 14,604 students from 24 universities. It reaches AUC 0.972 with external validation; SHAP highlights sleep, academic trajectory and social interaction.

title: Early warning and intervention for college students’ mental health status based on multimodal deep learning
summary_en: Proposes AMPAN, a multimodal deep network with attention that integrates survey and academic behaviour data of 3,500 college students over four semesters for early warning. It outperforms BiLSTM and multimodal Transformer baselines; attention maps increase counsellors' confidence.

title: Predicting and Analyzing Mental Health Risk and Characteristics of Young University Students Using Machine Learning and SHAP
summary_en: Identifies 14 factors qualitatively and compares several algorithms to predict mental health risk in university students. Gradient boosting with SHAP performs best; psychological attention, only-child status and interpersonal distress are the most influential factors.

title: Early Detection of Student Depression in India: A Proactive Approach to Preventing Suicidal Behaviors
summary_en: Compares several algorithms on an open Kaggle dataset to detect depression in Indian students, prioritising recall because of suicide risk. CatBoost and gradient boosting perform best; academic pressure, financial stress, suicidal thoughts and sleep are the main factors.

title: A Machine Learning Approach to Predicting Depression in University Students in Bangladesh: Enhancing Mental Health Assessment
summary_en: Predicts depression severity (PHQ-9) in 577 Bangladeshi university students with six classifiers. The voting classifier reaches 98.7% accuracy; privacy and consent are emphasised.

title: Addressing the Mental Health Crisis: Understanding Suicidal Risk Factors in University Students Through Interpretable Machine Learning
summary_en: Presents StudentSafe, a psychiatrist-validated dataset of 4,004 students from 99 universities, to predict suicide risk. XGBoost reaches F1 75.36%; LIME and SHAP point to device use, institution type, academic achievement and family environment.

title: A Machine Learning Framework for Early Depression Screening Based On Daily Activities
summary_en: Screens depression in 1,000 university students from daily habits (sleep, screen time, socialising, exercise, diet, study) with four models. XGBoost performs best (86.9%); SHAP highlights sleep quality, social interaction, screen time before bed and workload.

title: Early Detection of Mental Health Disorders Among Private University Students in Bangladesh Using Machine Learning-Based Behavioral Data Analysis
summary_en: Detects early signs of mental disorders in private university students from non-invasive behavioural data (sleep, study, digital activity) with deep tabular and boosting models. Tuned CatBoost reaches 99.79% accuracy.

title: Construction of the Text Sentiment Analysis Model for College Students’ Mental Health: Based on Machine Learning and Sentiment Dictionary
summary_en: Builds a sentiment analysis model (ML plus sentiment lexicon) on college students' social media texts to track emotional polarity and intensity and warn of crises. No metrics are reported.

title: A Four-Country Comparative Review on Stress, Anxiety, and Depression
summary_en: Four-country comparative review of stress, anxiety and depression in university students and the use of random forest and logistic regression. Reports AUC 0.74 and 0.77; finances, campus belonging, disability and age are the main predictors.

title: Intelligent Assessment of College Students’ Mental Health Based on Apriori Algorithm
summary_en: Proposes assessing college students' mental health with the Apriori algorithm (association rules), validated only by MATLAB simulation. Claims higher accuracy than conventional assessment without figures.

title: Analysis of College Students’ Mental Health Education Based on Machine Learning
screening_reason: Incoherent abstract: no data or analytic method described
summary_en: Claims to analyse college mental health education with machine learning and reports a 15-16% improvement, but the abstract does not describe data, method or design comprehensibly.

title: Research on the Prediction of Mental Health Problems of Vocational Students Based on Big Data and Deep Learning
summary_en: Uses big data and deep learning to identify psychological problems in vocational students. Claims an improvement above 10% without describing data or model.

title: AI-Driven Mental Health Prediction and Therapy for Early Adulthood: Relapse Prediction After Initial Treatment Response
screening_reason: Population: adults aged 18-40, not specifically students
summary_en: Classifies disorders (anxiety, depression, OCD, PTSD, sleep and eating disorders) in 200 adults aged 18-40 with four algorithms. XGBoost performs best (70%); emotional exhaustion, panic attacks and suicidal ideation are the most predictive features.

title: Early Detection and Support System for Student Mental Health Using Machine Learning
summary_en: Presents an early detection and support system that classifies anxiety and stress levels from activity logs and surveys. Logistic regression reaches 89.1%; the system includes automatic alerts and monitoring.

title: Predicting Suicide Ideation Among College Students in Karnataka Using Machine Learning
summary_en: Analyses suicidal ideation (ASIQ) in 689 college students in Karnataka with decision trees. Age, educational path, relationship problems, peer influence and drug use are the key factors.

title: Enhancing happiness and life satisfaction in university students: analysis with a machine learning approach
summary_en: Predicts happiness and life satisfaction in 816 university students from the China Family Panel Studies with external validation (724). Random forest and XGBoost perform best; SHAP shows interpersonal relationships and future confidence as the main predictors.

title: Predicting depression among public university students in Bangladesh using machine learning models
summary_en: Cross-sectional study of 500 students from 15 public universities: depression prevalence of 85.5%, associated with low CGPA, financial stress, lack of family support, ragging and session delays. SVM is the best model; SHAP highlights counselling services, the education system and session delays.

title: PMAP: A Multimodal Tool for Visual Analysis of Physiological Biomarkers and Audio for Student Mental Health
summary_en: Presents PMAP, a platform that visualises physiological biomarkers (heart rate, temperature, via Embrace Plus) and voice patterns to detect emotional crises. It does not yet include machine learning.

title: RETRACTED ARTICLE: Explainable artificial intelligence for predictive modeling of student stress in higher education
summary_en: RETRACTED. Classified student stress from surveys with six algorithms and SHAP (RF 0.89).

title: Prevalence, associated factors, and machine learning-based prediction of depression, anxiety, and stress among university students: a cross-sectional study from Bangladesh
summary_en: Measures prevalence (DASS-21) in 1,697 students from two public universities: depression 56.9%, anxiety 69.5%, stress 32.2%. Combines logistic regression with seven ML models, with only moderate performance; faculty and family relationships are the top predictors.

title: The influence of higher education based on machine learning on subjective well-being
screening_reason: General population (CGSS), not students; studies education as a factor
summary_en: Analyses with XGBoost and GBDT whether higher education increases subjective well-being in 53,874 Chinese residents (CGSS).

title: Student Health Risk Evaluator (SHRE): A Predictive Machine Learning Framework for Assessing Mental Health Risks in Students
summary_en: Proposes SHRE, a questionnaire-based risk evaluator with Lasso feature selection and four classifiers. Logistic regression reaches 94.12% accuracy.

title: The Effect of Secondary Traumatic Stress and Cognitive Flexibility on Psychological Well-Being in Health Education Students
summary_en: Examines in 620 nursing and midwifery students how secondary traumatic stress and cognitive flexibility affect psychological well-being (hierarchical regression and SHAP). Both explain 26.7% of the variance; cognitive flexibility is the most important.

title: Data Mining and Machine Learning based Student Mental Health Identification across Telangana Regions in India
summary_en: Proposes a platform with logistic regression, SVC and stacking to assess student mental health in Telangana and recommend interventions. No data or metrics are reported.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Predictive Analytics for Building Multi-dimensional Psychological Evaluation Models to Address Employment Stressors in College Students
summary_en: Relates age, working hours, sleep, PHQ-9 and PSS in 280 working college students with OLS regression, random forest and gradient boosting. Anxiety is the strongest predictor of stress; random forest has the lowest error.

title: Data-Driven Approach to Well Being Tracking in Language Education for Whole Person Learning
summary_en: Mixed-methods study of Microsoft Reflect (real-time emotional check-ins) in language classes at two universities. 80.3% of students improved emotional awareness, but the authenticity of digital emotional data is questioned.

title: Secure Storage Method of Students’ Mental Health Privacy Data Based on Machine Learning
screening_reason: Out of scope: data storage security, no analysis of well-being or mental health
summary_en: Proposes secure storage of students' mental health data by combining k-means with k-anonymity and encryption keys generated by a neural network. Reports lower information loss and faster decryption.

title: Advancing Mental Health Problems with Machine Learning and Genetic Algorithms for Anxiety Classification in Bangladeshi University Students
summary_en: Classifies anxiety levels in 1,977 students from 15 universities with eight algorithms and a genetic-algorithm-optimised logistic regression (99.49%). Academic pressure is the main factor.

title: Unveiling Academic Triumphs: Insights into Student Well-Being and Social Dynamics
summary_en: Relates happiness (Oxford Happiness Questionnaire), social support and academic performance (r = 0.79) and predicts academic success from trauma and addiction with a multilayer perceptron (79%).

title: Application of Machine Learning Algorithms to Mental Health Data Processing for College Students
summary_en: Applies C5.0 decision trees in SPSS to a college mental health database and compares them with SVM. C5.0 reaches 85% versus 83.12% for SVM.

title: Machine learning investigation of optimal psychoemotional well-being factors for students’ reading literacy
screening_reason: Out of scope: well-being is a predictor; the outcome is reading literacy
summary_en: Uses PISA 2018 (3,497 students from four Chinese regions) to identify which psychoemotional well-being factors distinguish high and low reading literacy. SVM with recursive feature elimination selects 15 of 25 factors (0.905).

title: Comprehensive analysis of stress factors affecting students: a machine learning approach
summary_en: Identifies stress factors in 1,100 students (StressLevelDataset) with correlation and random forest feature importance. Self-esteem and sleep quality are key predictors; anxiety correlates negatively with academic performance.

title: Impact of Music Teaching on Student Mental Health Using IoT, Recurrent Neural Networks, and Big Data Analytics
summary_en: Measures the effect of music education on mental health with IoT sensors (heart rate, environment) and LSTM recurrent networks. Reports 0.886 accuracy and personalised recommendations.

title: Framework for suggesting corrective actions to help students intended at risk of low performance based on experimental study of college students using explainable machine learning model
screening_reason: Main outcome is low academic performance
summary_en: Predicts students at risk of low performance with explainable ML, including personal, family and mental health factors, and proposes corrective actions. Accuracy exceeds 96.5%.

title: Identifying the top predictors of student well-being across cultures using machine learning and conventional statistics
summary_en: Analyses subjective well-being of 522,836 secondary students from 71 countries (PISA) with LightGBM and hierarchical linear models. School belonging and sense of meaning are common predictors across cultures.

title: Understanding Students’ Subjective and Eudaimonic Well-Being: Combining both Machine Learning and Classical Statistics
summary_en: Compares individual, family and school factors of subjective and eudaimonic well-being in 6,037 Hong Kong students (PISA 2018) with random forest and HLM. School belonging, parental support, resilience and fear of failure predict subjective well-being.

title: Proposal of a Machine Learning Model for the Early Detection of Depression in University Students
summary_en: Proposes a five-phase model for early depression detection in university students. Logistic regression reaches 0.81 accuracy and 0.85 sensitivity.

title: Data Analysis of Middle School Students’ Mental Health Test in Intelligent Security Management System
screening_reason: Title says middle school; text says university
summary_en: Uses association rules and decision trees on mental health test data in an intelligent management system to anticipate problems and intervene. After three months the share of students with failing scores drops by 13.41%.

title: Enhancing Machine Learning Approaches for Early Detection of Depression Levels for Vietnamese Students
summary_en: Seeks a culturally sensitive early depression diagnosis system for Vietnamese young people aged 15-25. No method or results are described.

title: Prediction Method of Higher Vocational Students’ Psychological Health Education Achievements Based on Big Data Mining Technology
screening_reason: Outcome is the grade in a mental health education course, not mental health
summary_en: Predicts grades in mental health education courses for vocational students with data mining and clustering on NoSQL.

title: RETRACTED ARTICLE: Exploring the influence of music education on the development of college mental health based on big data
summary_en: RETRACTED. Assessed the effect of music teaching on mental health with the SCL-90 and SQL Server.

title: Investigating the mental health of university students during the COVID-19 pandemic in a UK university: a machine learning approach using feature permutation importance
summary_en: Analyses mental well-being of UK university students during COVID-19 by applying permutation importance to several algorithms. Medical history and adversity worsen well-being; communication with family and friends and exercise improve it.

title: Understanding Chinese Students' Well-Being: A Machine Learning Study
summary_en: Uses PISA data on 12,058 Chinese 15-year-olds and random forest regression to explain four well-being dimensions. School belonging, resilience and fear of failure are the most important predictors.

title: Machine Learning, Wearable, and Smartphones for Student’s Mental Health Analysis
summary_en: Reviews studies applying ML, wearables and smartphones to student mental health, which technologies show most potential and which gaps remain.

title: Analysis of the Influence Factors of College Students’ Game Addiction Under the Background of Big Data Technology
summary_en: Studies online game addiction in 475 college students with regression and data mining. It differs by year, sex and only-child status; rumination partially mediates the link with negative life events.

title: Relationship of the Socioeconomic Conditions with the Emotional Well-Being of the Students of the Tecnológico Nacional de México Campus Tijuana: An Analysis Using Data Mining
summary_en: Relates social and family environment to emotional well-being and career satisfaction in 768 students of TecNM Tijuana using decision trees.

title: Extracting Attributes of Students Mental Health, Behaviour, Attendance and Performance in Academics During COVID-19 Pandemic using PCA Technique
screening_reason: Main focus is the effectiveness of online learning
summary_en: Analyses with PCA 30 factors (academic, behavioural, mental) from 224 students about online learning during COVID-19.

title: Practice of Big Data Technology and Improved BP Neural Network in College Students’ Mental Health Education
summary_en: Discusses the use of big data and BP neural networks for college mental health education through social media. No concrete data or results are described.
